confidence_rationale: An authoritative review of the readiness-potential literature establishing that the path from intention to executed movement is carried by neurally distinct, separately-modulable stages (early BP in pre-SMA/SMA ~2s before onset, reflecting subconscious readiness; late BP in M1/lateral premotor ~400ms before onset, modulated specifically by movement complexity). This supports Q-068's premise that graded action-statuses (rehearsed/intended/committed/acted) correspond to real, separable structural distinctions rather than arbitrary labels. Confidence is moderate because the BP axis maps onto the prepare->commit->execute tail of REE's gradient, not the simulated/rehearsed/intended distinctions at the covert end, and because human EEG of voluntary movement transfers only loosely to an agent's action-status annotation scheme.
failure_signatures: A model that treats 'about to act' as a single undifferentiated state cannot reproduce the early-BP / late-BP dissociation (different generators, different modulation by complexity); collapsing prepare and commit into one status loses a distinction the substrate actually makes.

The BP literature characterises the preparation-to-execution tail but is largely silent on the simulated-vs-rehearsed-vs-intended distinctions at the covert end of Q-068's gradient, and on self-reference-frame switching entirely.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The Bereitschaftspotential preceding self-initiated movement decomposes into an early component (beginning ~2s before onset in pre-SMA and SMA, site-non-specific, reflecting slowly increasing cortical excitability / subconscious readiness) and a late component (~400ms before onset in contralateral M1 and lateral premotor cortex, with precise somatotopy, selectively enhanced by movement complexity), i.e. preparation-to-execution is carried by temporally and anatomically distinct, differentially modulated stages.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-068 asks whether REE needs an explicit graded action-status vocabulary (simulated != rehearsed != intended != committed != acted) as a first-class annotation, or whether MECH-094 write-profiles plus the MECH-061 commit-boundary token already suffice. The BP evidence supports the premise that the later statuses (intended -> committed -> acted) are not a single state but neurally distinct stages, which argues that a graded annotation captures real structure -- the commit boundary (MECH-061) sits on a genuine transition (early->late BP / readiness->execution) rather than marking an arbitrary cut.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The BP indexes the preparation/commitment/execution tail of the gradient and says little about the covert end (simulated vs rehearsed vs intended) or about self_reference_frame switching; it shows the *later* statuses are separable but does not establish that REE must annotate the *full* five-way vocabulary as first-class rather than deriving the finer distinctions from write-profiles.
mapping.source_context: Human scalp EEG and epicortical recordings of self-initiated voluntary movement; movement-related cortical potentials.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality canonical review, but it covers only the prepare/commit/execute tail of Q-068's gradient; mapping fidelity is limited by silence on the covert-status distinctions and self-reference frames that are the harder part of the claim.
